chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the one confined (by illness) who did not bring the sacrificial animal, he said: 'He should perform the rituals and return. So if he cannot find the price of a sacrificial animal, he should fast.'

key_terms.الْمَحْصُورُ: The one confined or prevented from completing Hajj
key_terms.يَنْسُكُ: He performs the rituals (completes the rites)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim confined by illness who did not bring a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies the specific expiation for the *mahsur* (confined pilgrim) who omitted the *had* (sacrifice) due to inability, establishing fasting as the primary substitute when the financial means for an animal are absent. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations, distinguishing between the obligation to complete the Hajj rites and the separate duty of the sacrificial offering. The hadith underscores that the inability to perform a specific act of worship due to genuine constraint removes the burden of its full form, replacing it with a manageable alternative.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the one confined (by an illness) not ushering the sacrificial animal: ‘He should perform rituals and return. So if he cannot find the price of a sacrificial animal, he should Fast’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

This is about a man who has become al-Mahsur (confined) and has not driven an offering. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He completes all other acts and returns home, and if he cannot pay for the offering, he must fast.’”
